chapter: Chicago, Lee Collins and the road
title: Teenage spasm band in the District and Decatur Street honky-tonks
summary: At 16 or 17 Danny led a six-piece spasm band with tin pans, washboard and kazoo and promoted his own gigs.

story.theme_name: First paying gigs: getting started as a young professional
story.community_name: First paid gigs: pay, bands and young beginnings

blocks.x: And there was so much for you to see in this town. You saw a big ocean liner, you'd see all these Oriental people coming in here on those ships. And we began to play in the nightclubs and the little honky-tonks on Decatur Street. When I was 16 and 17, I didn't use(?) any (?)s. We had ...(?)... out in the District with a Spasm band, and we used to... I used to take the kids out, and became a little promoter myself. I found out if you want something done, you have to do it yourself. I learned that early. And I had
this little Spasm band, about six of us, we'd play...
So you call it a Spasm band.
That's what they called it. You know, those makeshift bands?

Cats take a box and put some tin pans on it, and there are big jar covers like cymbals, three or four of them together. They're noisemakers! And we had a cowbell on that. And one of them had a washboard. They'd have a kazoo. We'd have a ukelele or a guitar. And you'd go in and sing the songs! We sang the (?) to "Chinaman and Mabel." Did I do that for you?
Yeah, you did that. You sang it, but you couldn't remember all the words to it.
